+BOUNDS AND COVERAGE OF THE VERIFICATION
+=======================================
+
+Claim: For all integers x, (x + 1) * (x - 1) = x^2 - 1
+Spec (spec.txt): forall x : Z. (x + 1) * (x - 1) = x * x - 1
+
+1. DOMAIN OF THE CLAIM
+   The claim quantifies over ALL integers Z: an infinite (countably),
+   unbounded domain in both directions. It makes no restriction to
+   positive values, machine-width integers, or any finite range.
+
+2. PROOF METHOD AND ITS COVERAGE
+   Method: deductive proof (proof.txt) from stated axioms
+   (commutativity of + and *, distributivity, subtraction as addition
+   of the additive inverse), applied to an arbitrary x, closed by
+   universal generalization.
+   Coverage: COMPLETE with respect to the axioms used. The derivation
+   holds for every x : Z, including values outside any tested range,
+   because no step depends on the particular value of x.
+
+   Qualification (from audit.txt): the proof additionally relies on
+   ring facts of Z beyond the four permitted axioms - multiplicative
+   unit (Z2), annihilator (Z3), additive unit (Z4), and associativity
+   of + as a regrouping convention (Z5). Under the standard reading
+   that these are part of the structure of Z, the proof is sound; under
+   a strict "four axioms only" reading, the proof is incomplete.
+
+3. CHECKER METHOD AND ITS COVERAGE
+   Method: brute-force testing (counterexample_check.py) of
+   x = -100 .. 100 (201 values), comparing (x+1)*(x-1) with x*x - 1
+   using exact Python integer arithmetic (no overflow).
+   Coverage: FINITE and PARTIAL. It covers only 201 of the infinitely
+   many integers. It can refute the claim (a single failure would be a
+   genuine counterexample) but can never establish it: passing tests
+   provide inductive evidence only, not proof.
+
+4. LIMITATIONS OF THE CHECKER
+   - Range bound: values with |x| > 100 are untested; a hypothetical
+     counterexample there would be missed.
+   - Not a proof: agreement on a finite set does not imply agreement
+     on Z.
+   - Fixed range: the bounds -100 and 100 are hard-coded; rerunning
+     with a different range changes coverage but never achieves
+     completeness.
+   - Oracle identity: the checker evaluates both sides as Python
+     expressions; it verifies the identity as computed, which assumes
+     Python's arbitrary-precision integers faithfully model Z (valid
+     here, since only +, *, - are used and no overflow occurs).
+   - Structural scope: the checker tests a single fixed equation; it
+     does not parse or validate spec.txt, proof.txt, or the axioms.
+
+5. OVERALL ASSESSMENT
+   - The deductive proof is the load-bearing verification; subject to
+     the axiom qualification in audit.txt, it establishes the claim
+     for all of Z.
+   - The brute-force check is corroborating evidence only: it confirms
+     the claim on [-100, 100] and found no counterexamples
+     (201/201 matches), consistent with the proof.
+   - Together: claim established for all integers, with empirical
+     corroboration limited to the tested range.
